docs.subtitle: National Disability Insurance Scheme (Quality Indicators for NDIS Practice Standards) Guidelines 2018, section 10. Compilation 3, in force 1 July 2026. Rules Schedule 1, clause 7.
docs.html:
1Outcome

Each participant accesses supports free from violence, abuse, neglect, exploitation or discrimination.

2Quality indicators

(1)

Policies, procedures and practices are in place which actively prevent violence, abuse, neglect, exploitation or discrimination.

(2)

Each participant is provided with information about the use of an advocate (including an independent advocate) and access to an advocate is facilitated where allegations of violence, abuse, neglect, exploitation or discrimination have been made.

(3)

Allegations and incidents of violence, abuse, neglect, exploitation or discrimination, are acted upon, each participant affected is supported and assisted, records are made of any details and outcomes of reviews and investigations (where applicable) and action is taken to prevent similar incidents occurring again.

sections: Section B: The decision to report (child safety lead)
Section C: The report (the person who made it)
Section D: The family and the child's supports (child safety lead)
Section E: Follow-up and closing (child safety lead)

questions.hint: Give their full name, the name they like to be called and their date of birth. Add, from REG-ECS-01 col G: the family's language and interpreter need, how the child communicates, and whether the family identifies as Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander, as they have told us. The child safety lead adds their record number in REG-ECS-01.

questions.text: What is the incident report number, or is this not an incident?
questions.hint: Where the harm is connected with our supports or one of our workers, take the number from question 19 of FRM-INC-01 when the Quality Manager gives it, and write "not yet given" until then. Where it is not connected with our supports, write "not an incident: not connected with our supports". The child safety lead completes this.

questions.text: What kind of concern is it?
questions.hint: Choose every kind that worries you. You do not need proof. "Harm connected with our supports or one of our workers" makes the concern an incident as well.

options: harm connected with our supports or one of our workers

questions.text: Why do you suspect the child is at risk of harm?
questions.hint: Where the concern is not an incident, this is the full account: what happened, in order, facts only; the child's exact words; the time; who else was there. Where the concern is also an incident, the full account is at question 7 of FRM-INC-01; give a few lines here and do not copy it.
Choose the closest group. The name is at question 11 of FRM-INC-01. Write "not known" if nobody is identified.

options: a parent, carer or family member
one of our workers, managers or owners

questions.hint: Think about the child's brothers and sisters, other children in the home or setting, and other participants. Write "nobody identified" with your reason if that is so.

questions.section: Section B: The decision to report (child safety lead)
questions.text: Do you suspect on reasonable grounds that the child is at risk of harm? Where the law of [state or territory] sets belief as the test, suspicion is the lower bar
questions.hint: A reasonable suspicion is enough. Proof is not needed. Note the date and time of the worker's call. If you are unsure, phone the child protection authority for advice before you answer, and write the advice at question 8.

controls.label: Then the reason, and the date and time of the worker's call

questions.section: Section B: The decision to report (child safety lead)
questions.text: If no report was made, why not, who decided and what advice was taken?
questions.hint: Give the name and role of the person who decided, the advice and who gave it, and the date and time. A "no" with no reason cannot be defended.
questions.optional: Yes, only when a report was made

questions.section: Section C: The report (the person who made it)
questions.text: Which authority was told, how, and when?
questions.hint: Give the name of the authority. Say whether you phoned or used its online report. Give the date and time.
questions.optional: Yes, only when no report was made

questions.section: Section C: The report (the person who made it)
questions.text: Who made the report, and what is the reference number?
questions.hint: Give the name, role and phone number of the person who made it. Ask the authority for a reference number. Write "none given" and the time you asked if it gave none.
questions.optional: Yes, only when no report was made

questions.section: Section C: The report (the person who made it)
questions.text: What did you tell the authority?
questions.hint: Give the facts you gave, in a few lines. Leave out opinions.
questions.optional: Yes, only when no report was made

questions.section: Section C: The report (the person who made it)
questions.text: What did the authority tell you to do?
questions.hint: Include any instruction about the family, the child, police, our workers or keeping things as they are. Give the name of the person you spoke to.
questions.optional: Yes, only when no report was made

questions.section: Section D: The family and the child's supports (child safety lead)
questions.text: Was the family told about the report?
questions.hint: Tell a person with parental responsibility, unless that could put the child at risk or the authority or police ask you not to. Ask the authority first when the concern is about someone in the home.

options: not told, it could put the child at risk
not told, the authority or police asked us not to

controls.label: Then who was told or who decided, the advice taken, and the date and time

questions.section: Section D: The family and the child's supports (child safety lead)
questions.text: How are the child's supports carrying on?
questions.hint: Say which sessions, settings or workers changed, what replaced them, and whether this followed the continuity arrangement in REG-ECS-01 col Y. Give the date the family agreed. Write "no change" if supports carry on as before.

questions.section: Section D: The family and the child's supports (child safety lead)
questions.text: If the concern is about one of our workers, managers or owners, who is handling it?
questions.hint: Give the name and role of the person handling it, the date the person the concern is about was moved away from child contact, the date they were told, and the FRM-SGD-01 number. Moving away is not a finding.
questions.optional: Yes, only when the concern is about one of our workers, managers or owners

questions.section: Section E: Follow-up and closing (child safety lead)
questions.text: What did the authority or police do or ask of us, and when?
questions.hint: Add a dated entry for each contact, and one for each other body told at PRO-ECS-02 step 19: the body, the date and time, who told them and the reference number. Ask the authority for the outcome. Write "no response" and the date you asked if there is none.

questions.section: Section E: Follow-up and closing (child safety lead)
questions.text: Was every report and notice made inside our times?
questions.hint: Check the time limits at steps 14, 16, 17, 19, 20, 21 and 23 of PRO-ECS-02. If any was late, say which, how late and why. Say when the Chief Executive was told.

controls.label: Then which one, how late, why, and the date and time the Chief Executive was told

questions.section: Section E: Follow-up and closing (child safety lead)
questions.text: What changed in the child's risk assessment and support plan, and when?
questions.hint: Give the date of each change and whether the family agreed. Write "no change needed" and the reason if none.

questions.section: Section E: Follow-up and closing (child safety lead)
questions.text: Is this record ready to close?
questions.hint: Close it only when no action is due from us to the authority or police, every notice is recorded, the family was told or the reason is recorded, and the child's supports are settled. Give the date and who approved.

form.intro:
Use this record for every concern that a child is at risk of harm, from anyone, in any place. It shows why we suspect, on reasonable grounds, that the child is at risk. It shows the report made to the child protection authority of [state or territory], and what happened next.

  • Section A: the practitioner who has the concern completes this the same day.
  • Section B: the child safety lead completes this during the worker's first call.
  • Section C: the person who made the report to the authority completes this. That is the worker, or the child safety lead.
  • Sections D and E: the child safety lead completes these as the concern is managed.

This record sits beside the incident report only where the harm is connected with the provision of our supports or with one of our workers (PRO-ECS-02 Decision table 2). In that case the worker's account of what happened goes on FRM-INC-01 Incident Report Form, as for any incident, and question 4 here is a short reason only. Where the concern is not connected with our supports, there is no incident report and no NDIS Commission notice: question 4 carries the full account.

Phone the child safety lead before you start writing. If a child is in danger, call 000 first.

Have ready: the child's name, date of birth and address, and the names of the people who live with them. Have the reference number the authority gave you.

What happens next: the child safety lead gives this record a number and enters it in REG-ECS-01 col J. PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets every step. When systems are down, use the paper copy kept at [location at each site].
form.privacy:
We collect this information to keep a child safe and to make reports under child protection law. We also collect it to meet our duties under the NDIS Act 2013.

Only the child safety lead, the deputy and the Chief Executive read it. The Quality Manager and auditors read REG-INC-01 and REG-ECS-01 col J, not this form. The plan lead and the Service Manager receive only the outcome for the child's supports and plan (questions 14 and 18), by note. We give parts of it to the child protection authority, police, the NDIS Commission and other bodies. We do this when the law requires or allows it. A report to the authority needs no consent.

A person with parental responsibility can ask what we hold about their child. We may hold back parts if giving them could put the child at risk. We also hold back parts if the law or an authority tells us not to. We remove other people's details first. We never tell the person a concern is about who raised it. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store and protect this record.
form.after:
• Practitioner: phone the child safety lead first. Give Section A to the child safety lead, and to nobody else, the same day (our standard).
  • If the concern is about the child safety lead, give it to the deputy. If it is about the deputy, give it to the lead. If it is about a manager, give it to the lead and the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive or an owner, give it to the chair of the governing body. In a sole trader's business, give it to the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register.
  • You can also report straight to the child protection authority or the NDIS Commission. POL-GOV-03 Whistleblower and Disclosure Protection Policy sets out how you are protected.
  • Child safety lead: complete Section B within 1 hour of the worker's call (our standard).
  • Child safety lead: give the record its number and enter it in REG-ECS-01 col J the same day (our standard).
  • Child safety lead: complete Section D within 1 business day of the concern (our standard).
  • Child safety lead: add dated entries to Section E until the record is closed. Read every open record at least every 20 business days (our standard).
  • Keep the closed record in the restricted section of the child's file. Keep it for 45 years from the day it is made (Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, recommendation 8.1; check the records law of [state or territory] at adoption). Where the concern is also an incident, the Incident Rules, section 12(4), minimum of 7 years applies as well. REG-ECS-01 sets the same period for the row where col J holds this record's number.

signs.confirms: "I have written why I am worried, as accurately as I can."

signs.who: The child safety lead: name, signature
signs.confirms: The decision to report is recorded with its reason

signs.who: The person who made the report: name, role, signature
signs.confirms: "I made this report, and I have written what I told the authority and what I was told."

signs.who: The child safety lead: name, signature. The Chief Executive also signs to close a concern about one of our workers, managers or owners
signs.confirms: Every notice is recorded and the record meets the closing conditions
